arguments.value: Patient presented with one week of progressive throbbing headache, vomiting, sudden-onset weakness that progressed from the right lower limb to the right upper limb and then bilaterally, and a generalized tonic-clonic seizure, with severe depressed consciousness requiring ventilation. Examination showed extensor plantar responses and absent pupillary reflexes; fundoscopy was normal. MRA revealed multiple dural arteriovenous fistulas involving the sigmoid and transverse sinuses with feeders from the bilateral external carotid arteries and right internal carotid artery, with retrograde flow. He was treated with mannitol, levetiracetam, and transarterial cyanoacrylate glue embolization, leading to partial neurological recovery and good status at two-month follow-up.
